project_size.unit: physical source lines of code (excluding comments and blank lines)

methodology.identifier_normalization: Case-insensitive matching; uppercase unique GHSA/CVE identifier sets; no IDs inferred from titles or code.
methodology.anchor_identifiers: Union of identifiers on associated retained entries and their reports.
methodology.identifier_limitations: Identifier counts are not independent vulnerability counts; one report may reference multiple GHSA IDs, and CVE and GHSA can identify the same advisory.
methodology.categories: Original L1/L2 labels are preserved. Entry counts count rows; report counts count distinct (report_id, category) memberships. Percentages use the scope's entry count or distinct report count, so report percentages can sum above 100 if a report has multiple labels.
methodology.language: Measured code SLOC per language at each pinned snapshot; primary language has most code SLOC, with alphabetical language-name tie breaking.
methodology.language_entry_counts: Each entry inherits its snapshot's primary language; this is not the language of its vulnerable anchor.
methodology.language_snapshot_coverage: A language covers a snapshot only when its code SLOC is positive; multilingual coverage counts need not sum to the snapshot count.
methodology.project_identity: Exact repo_url; repeated commits are distinct snapshots of the same repository.
methodology.size_limitations: snapshot_sloc_sum and language SLOC sum count multiple revisions of a project; neither is deduplicated project source volume.

policy.generated_header_pattern: (?im)^\s*(?://|#|/\*|\*|<!--)\s*(?:code generated[^\n]*do not edit|this file (?:is|was) generated by|(?:this file (?:is|was) )?(?:<?auto[- ]?generated|automatically generated)|@generated)\b
notes: Only regular files tracked by the exact source commit are eligible; symlinks and submodules are not followed.
Programming, template and style languages in the explicit allowlist count toward SLOC; documentation, data and configuration languages do not.
Test, example and benchmark source files are included unless another explicit exclusion applies.

Vendored/generated exclusions use path rules, Git attributes, an anchored generated-file header and cloc --no-autogen. These are heuristic rules, not a claim that every generated file is identifiable.
SLOC is cloc physical code lines excluding blank and comment lines. Each tracked path counts separately, even when contents are identical.
